description: Render `frames` frames of the project (or `scene`) in a separate movie-writer run: no bridge, session or input (to interact: run_project, simulate_input). mode check (default): stats, likelyBlank, motion, inline frames, files deleted. frames: keeps PNGs. video: .avi/.ogv, no stats. Returns: frameCount, likelyBlank, anyMotion, samples, paths, bytesWritten; warnings leads if unmeasured or unconfirmed. Needs a display; asks the user once per project. Errors on timeout, failed run or live session.

format.description: [video] Movie container (default "avi"). "ogv" needs an engine that can write it; the error names the format and engine version when it cannot. Rejected in other modes.

fps.description: Fixed simulation and capture rate (default 30, max 120). Game time covered is frames / fps seconds, whatever the wall-clock speed.

frames.description: Frames to render before Godot quits (default 30, max 600). The first frames can be blank while the scene loads; likelyBlank is judged on the last one. The run is budgeted at 30s plus 250ms per frame, and a run that overruns it takes up to 10s more to stop. A run of 77 to 80 frames is refused, with nothing run, because its answer would not fit a client's 60s request timeout; above that a client may cut the call off before this server can report a timeout.

inlineFrames.description: [check] Inline images to return, evenly spaced and ending at the last frame (default 3, max 6; 0 for none). Each is downscaled to fit 960x540; stats are measured at full size. Rejected in other modes.

mode.description: "check" (default) measures a sample of frames, returns a few inline, and deletes every file. "frames" keeps the PNG sequence (and frame.wav) under .mcp/godot-runtime/movies/ and returns paths plus stats for a sample. "video" writes one movie file and returns its path; it has no pixel stats.

projectPath.description: Path to the Godot project directory

scene.description: Scene to render (path relative to project, e.g. "scenes/main.tscn"). Omit to use the project's main scene. Must end in .tscn, .scn, .escn, .tres or .res.

name: render_movie

anyMotion.description: True when some pair of consecutive measured frames had at least its motionThreshold of pixels whose R, G or B changed by more than 8 of 255; every pixel is compared. Null when no measured pair moved and a pair was not measured, or fewer than two frames were measured. motionPairs has the counts behind it.

bytesWritten.description: Total size in bytes of every file this run wrote under .mcp/godot-runtime/movies/. In check mode the files are deleted again (framesKept false); in frames and video mode they stay on disk until removed by hand. Null when the run directory could not be read.

frameCount.description: PNG frames found on disk after the run.

framePaths.description: Omitted above 60 frames; use framePattern and frameCount.

likelyBlank.description: Judged on every pixel of the last frame: true when it is one flat colour (no channel varies by more than 8 of 255 across it). Null when it was not measured.

measuredFrames.description: Sampled frames whose stats were measured.

motion.description: Largest mean RGB difference between consecutive measured frames, over every pixel, 0 to 1. A small mover reads near 0 here; anyMotion is decided by the changed pixel count, not by this mean.

changedBounds.description: Smallest rectangle holding every changed pixel, in frame pixels from the top left. Null when no pixel changed or the pair was not measured.

changedFraction.description: changedPixels divided by the pixels in the frame, 0 to 1. Null exactly where difference is null.

changedPixels.description: Pixels where R, G or B changed by more than 8 of 255. Null exactly where difference is null.

difference.description: Mean absolute RGB difference over every pixel, 0 to 1.

motionThreshold.description: The changedPixels count this pair needed to show motion: 4 up to a 1152x648 frame, more in proportion to the pixels of a larger one. Null exactly where difference is null.

statsAvailable.description: False in video mode: stats need PNG frames.
